pages.title: Data transfer Instructions
pages.text:
Data transfer Instructions:
Move destination, source
Source can be register, memory location,
immediate operand
both can't be memory location at the same time
stack operations:
Push AX - Pop AX - Pusha AX - Popa AX
AX can be any register, memory location
address transfer:
LEA register, Source
LEA Bx, [DI] <-> mov Bx, offset [DI]
To Get the address of DI "first char" and store it in BX
Arithmetic Instructions:
- ADD destination, Source
with add operation we can add byte to byte or word to word. Like
ADD Ax, cx <-> Its correct
ADD CL, DL <-> Its correct
byte to word is wrong
8 bits 16 bits
I/ Carry flag CF=1 then active
- ADC AX, LSL <-> AX = AX + LSL + I
- INC source: increase register or source by 1
if Ax=8 INC Ax -> Ax=9
- AAA -> It correct the content of AL
For Subtraction:
- SUB Destination, source
SUB AX, 4H -> Ax = Ax - 4H
- DEC source: decrease source by 1
- NEG source: change the sign of the source (opposite sign)

pages.title: I2207 - SBB, CMP, MUL
pages.text:
I2207 (2) 11.5.2025

- SBB destination, source: Subtract with Borrow/carry
Like if the Carry flag CF = 1 it decrement the
answer by 1
& Mov AX, 12H / first we make AX = 12 H
SCF / this change the value of CF from 0 to 1
SBB AX, 5 / subtract Ax - (1x + 5) = 6 H
- CMP destination, source : Compare two specific
bytes of words and do an instruction according
to the result
CMP AX, 7H / this compares AX with 7 by subtracting them
JNZ end; / if not zero jump to end
For multiplication:
- MUL source: it multiply byte by byte or word by word
1. if source is 1 byte then AL is
multiplied by it and stored in AX
2. if source is word then Ax is
multiplied by it and stored in DX:AX
(DX is upper) (AX is lower)
- IMUL source:
Same as MUL but it consider signs
For Division:
- DIV source: it divides word by byte or double-word by word
if source is 1 byte, AX is divided by source and
quotient = AL & remainder = AH

pages.title: Division and variable declaration
pages.text:
if source is word, (DX:AX) is divided by source,
and AX = quotient DX = remainder
- IDIV: it is signed division instruction
Variable declaration in assembly:
DB: Define byte (8 bits) / x db ? (uninitialized variable)
DW: Define word (16 bits) / x dw 5 Y db 3
DD: Define double word (32 bits)
DP: 6 bits
DQ: Define Quad word (64 bits)
Read/Input Variables:
To enter a character with the keyboard we do:
Mov AH, 1 -> the function 1 is to read character
int 21h -> interrupt 21h
The input is stored in AL. And the number is stored
as a character to use it as a number:
Sub AL, 48 OR sub AL, '0'
mov AH, 7 / when we use 7 it read but
int 21h / it does not display character we entered
Write or Display:
mov DL, 'A' / you move the character you want
mov AH, 2 / to display to DL and then do this
int 21h / we can read only one digit at a time
Display a message:
mov DX, offset variable or Lea DX, variable
mov ah, 9 -> to display a message
int 21h

pages.title: If, else Condition and Logical Instructions
pages.text:
I2207 (3) 17.5.2025

- If, else Condition:
we use cmp to solve if-else in assembly
cmp source, destination / to get the result of cmp then
jxy address of Lable / jump to address of Lable
jl: jump if less, jle: jump if less or equal, jc: jump if carry
jne: jump if not equal, jg: jump if greater, jge: jump if greater
or equal, jnz: jump if not equal zero, jz: jump if equal zero
If we need to use jump without any condition we
use jmp address of Lable
Logical instructions:
- Not source: convert all the bits in a byte or
word ex. 00110110 -> 11001001
- And destination, source: do and operation over all bits
- OR destination, source: or operation on bits
- XOR destination, source: xor operation on bits
if you have trouble understanding this check page 5, week 3
Shift instruction:
- SHL destination, count (shift left)
It moves the most left bit to AL=10110110 -> SHL AL, 1
the left and add zero at 01101100 -> CF=1
the beginning and add the moved bit in CF
- SHR destination, count (shift right)
same as SHL but in the other direction / Like AL=10010111
SHR res=01001011 CF=1

pages.title: Shift Arithmetic and Loops
pages.text:
- SAR source, count (shift Arithmetic right)
we add the new bit according to AL=10111001
the sign of the number, if it is negative SAR AL, 3
it starts and adds 1s else it add 0s AL=11110111
- SAL destination, count (shift arithmetic left)
Same as SAR
Rotate instruction:
- Rol destination, count (Rotate left)
it rotate the bits in a byte or word / Ax=10110111
so the left bit become the right and Rol Bx, 1
it is also added to the CF also -> 01101111 CF=1
- RoR destination, count (Rotate right)
Same as Rol
- RCL destination, count (Rotate through carry Left)
In this instruction the first left bit is stored in the CF and the previous CF is added as the first right bit
- RCR
Same as RCL
Loop:
- for: cmp cl, 4
jg end loop
add s, cl
inc cl
jmp for
end loop:
- while: cmp si, 4
jg endwhile
add s, si
inc si
jmp while
end while:

pages.title: Propositional Logic and Semantic Tableaux
pages.text:
I2209 (1) 19.5.2025

Proposition: can be writen "p,q,r..." and it is a proposed statement
Logical connections:
- And (&): add two propositions and it is true when both are true
- or (v): will be true if either p or q are true
- if-then (->): if p true then q should be true "called implies"
- If and only if (<->): this is true when p and q are the
same either true or false
- Negation - Not (~):
Tautologies & consistency:
- Tautology iff V(A) = T with any formula
- consistent iff V(A) = T for one where it is true
- inconsistent iff V(A) = F for all
Logical consequence: A |= B iff V(A) = T then V(B) = T
Logical equivalences: A == B iff A |= B and B |= A
* Page 39 in pdf for memorize (the last one rule in both columns are True?)
Note: |= (tautology)
|= (logical consequence)
Semantic Tableau system:

~ | ^ | v | -> | <->
~ ~ p
------
p | p ^ q
-----
p
q | p v q
-----
/ \
p   q | p -> q
------
/ \
~p  q | p <-> q
-------
/   \
p     ~p
q     ~q
 | ~(p ^ q)
--------
/ \
~p  ~q | ~(p v q)
--------
~
p
~
q | ~(p -> q)
---------
p
~q | ~(p <-> q)
----------
/ \
p  ~p
~q  q

It is better to start with stack first
Set is inconsistent if all branches close
Set is consistent if at least one branch is open

pages.title: Rules of inference and Resolution
pages.text:
branch is closed if there is x & ~x in the same root.
Rules of inference:
- Modus Ponens (law of detachment - mode that affirms):
if a conditional statement and its hypothesis are true
then the conclusion must also be true
p -> q -> condition statement
p -> hypothesis
.: q -> therefore evaluation
Important table page 72 (Rules of inference)
- Satisfiability (SAT) and Propositional resolution
p -> q
q -> r
------
.: p -> r
literal is: p or ~p
clause is: p or ~p or p v q v r
Conversion to clausal:
- p v q -> {p, q}
- p ^ q -> {p}, {q}
The empty clause is unsatisfiable
Proof by refutation or contradiction:
A |= B iff A U {~B} is unsatisfiable
to prove that A logical consequence of B we should
take the negation of the conclusion (~B) and prove that
it leads to an empty clause.
How to prove
{p -> q, q -> r} |= p -> r ?
1. convert this to clausal
p -> q => {~p, q}
q -> r => {~q, r}
~(p -> r) => {p}, {~r}
then number them
and last derive them from each other

pages.title: Processor control instructions and Loops
pages.text:
I2207 (4) 23.5.2025

Processor control instructions:
STC: Set Carry flag to 1
STD: Set direction flag to 1
STI: Set Interrupt flag to 1
CLC: clear Carry flag to 0
CLD: clear direction flag to 0
CLI: clear interrupt flag to 0
CMC: Complement CF
Note: JNC means if CF = 0, JNS means if SF = 0
SF: get the bit in the MSB, after an operation (add, sub)
so we can determine the sign of a number
PF: if the number of 1 bits is even then it is set to 1
if the number is odd then it is cleared to 0
AF: contains the carry but from the fourth bit to the fifth
Loop Instructions:
First we should define CX (Count) the rate of repetition and
then start the loop ex. for:
Loop for
and the CX value will automatically decrease by 1 each loop
without do it that manually
Do-While loop:
same as for but use do -----
Loop do
Array:
A db 10 dup(0); create an array of 10 elements and fill them with 0
A db 10,2,7,6
A dw 2,3,12
Only si & di can be used to indicate an element in array A[si], A[di]
to move to a new line when display use: new dw 10,13,'$'
